hints: A Cartesian plane equation can be found from a normal vector perpendicular to two independent directions in the plane.
Form two vectors using the given points, for example $\overrightarrow{CB}=(2,1,0)$ and $\overrightarrow{CD}=(1,0,5)$.
Take their cross product, or solve scalar-product equations, to obtain a normal proportional to $(5,-10,-1)$.
Substitute any of $B,C,D$ into $5x-10y-z=d$ to determine the constant.
walkthrough:
State the position vectors of the three points forming plane $BCD$:
$$\overrightarrow{OB} = 3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \overrightarrow{OC} = \mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \overrightarrow{OD} = 2\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} + 5\mathbf{k} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$$

Find two displacement vectors lying in the plane:
$$\overrightarrow{CB} = \overrightarrow{OB} - \overrightarrow{OC} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\overrightarrow{CD} = \overrightarrow{OD} - \overrightarrow{OC} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the normal vector $\mathbf{n}$ using the cross product $\overrightarrow{CB} \times \overrightarrow{CD}$:
$$\mathbf{n} = \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 \end{vmatrix}$$
$$= \mathbf{i}\bigl((1)(5) - (0)(0)\bigr) - \mathbf{j}\bigl((2)(5) - (0)(1)\bigr) + \mathbf{k}\bigl((2)(0) - (1)(1)\bigr)$$
$$= 5\mathbf{i} - 10\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -10 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$
Write the plane equation in the form $5x - 10y - z = d$.

Find $d$ by substituting point $C(1, 3, 0)$:
$$d = 5(1) - 10(3) - 1(0) = 5 - 30 = -25$$
Check with point $B(3, 4, 0)$:
$$5(3) - 10(4) - 1(0) = 15 - 40 = -25 \quad \text{(consistent)}$$
Check with point $D(2, 3, 5)$:
$$5(2) - 10(3) - 1(5) = 10 - 30 - 5 = -25 \quad \text{(consistent)}$$

State the Cartesian equation of plane $BCD$:
$$5x - 10y - z = -25 \quad \left(\text{or } -5x + 10y + z = 25\right)$$

hints: The acute angle between planes is found from their normal vectors.
Use the normal from part (i), $(5,-10,-1)$, and note that plane $OABC$ is $z=0$ with normal $(0,0,1)$.
Apply the scalar-product formula with an absolute value and divide by both normal magnitudes before taking the inverse cosine.
walkthrough:
Determine the normal vector to plane $OABC$:
The points $O(0, 0, 0)$, $A(3, 0, 0)$, $B(3, 4, 0)$, and $C(1, 3, 0)$ all lie in the $xy$-plane ($z = 0$).
Therefore, the unit normal vector to plane $OABC$ is along the $z$-axis:
$$\mathbf{n}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \mathbf{k}$$

State the normal vector to plane $BCD$ from part (i):
$$\mathbf{n}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -10 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Calculate the magnitude of each normal vector:
$$|\mathbf{n}_1| = 1$$
$$|\mathbf{n}_2| = \sqrt{5^2 + (-10)^2 + (-1)^2} = \sqrt{25 + 100 + 1} = \sqrt{126}$$

Calculate the cosine of the acute angle $\theta$ between the planes:
$$\cos\theta = \dfrac{|\mathbf{n}_1 \cdot \mathbf{n}_2|}{|\mathbf{n}_1||\mathbf{n}_2|} = \dfrac{|-1|}{1 \times \sqrt{126}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{126}}$$

Compute the decimal value and angle:
$$\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{126}} \approx \dfrac{1}{11.224972} \approx 0.089087$$
$$\theta = \cos^{-1}(0.089087) \approx 84.889^\circ \approx 84.9^\circ \quad (\text{or } 1.48 \text{ radians})$$
